chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah and al-Hakam ibn Miskeen from Jamil and Ibn Bukayr
Regarding the child of a free man and a slave woman, he said: 'The lineage goes to the free one of the two.'
ai.seo_question: Who does the child's lineage follow in a mixed-status union between a free man and a slave woman?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the principle of *ibn al-umm* (child of the slave woman), establishing that the child's lineage (*nasab*) follows the free parent, thereby inheriting their social status. In Shia jurisprudence, this ruling ensures the child is not bound to the mother's slavery, facilitating their eventual emancipation and full integration into the free community. The narration highlights the importance of distinguishing between the mother's status and the father's in determining the child's legal identity.
